- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per subsequent period to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate bullishness; apply 0.5–1.5% downward correction to forecast.  
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (≥3/30d) and bearish sentiment persists, forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–2% per event to reflect supply pressure.  
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong spikes; if price exceeds 75% of 30d high, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per period until price stabilizes.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate price stability; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid false confidence.
